issue.title: In-process TUI restarts report cumulative app_construct_seconds (50/100/147 s)

task_type_fields.impact: Startup-stage grading reads garbage after any in-process restart. The sase-1t3 soak-verify stage table had to grade Construction from the first startup row only. A perf runbook reader or `tui_freeze_report` consumer comparing construction across restarts would see a fake 50-150 s regression.
task_type_fields.repro:
`_mark_app_construct_start()` in `src/sase/ace/tui/util/startup_clock.py:98-102` only sets the module global `_app_construct_start_mono` when it is `None`, while `_app_construct_end_mono` is overwritten on every construct. In a process that constructs `AceApp` more than once (the `sase tui --restart-service` in-process restart path), `pre_mount_split_fields()` reports `app_construct_seconds` as the time since the *first* construct start.

Evidence in `~/.sase/logs/tui_startup.jsonl` on athena (pid 471245, build 194b1a1ef4, 2026-11-18T23:07-23:10Z): consecutive startup rows from one process report `app_construct_seconds` 1.094, 50.88, 100.83, 147.59 s. Each restart adds the elapsed wall time since the first construct. A fresh process on the same build (pid 3820644, 23:12:45Z) reports 0.458 s.

Repro: run `sase tui --restart-service`, restart in-process twice, then `jq -c 'select(.pid==<pid>) | .app_construct_seconds' ~/.sase/logs/tui_startup.jsonl`. Fix: reset the construct-start anchor per construct (or per app instance), and add a test that two constructs in one process each report their own duration. Check whether `_compose_start_mono` and the other anchors share the bug.

issue.creation_reason: Found while landing epic sase-1t3: restart-service rows on the same build reported 50-147 s construction while a fresh process took 0.46 s, which corrupts the startup telemetry the epic's soak grades against.
